title: The Single Entity
summary: Introduces single-entity data modeling, translation of a model into one relational table, and SQL for defining, querying, and maintaining that table.

concepts.title: Entities and attributes
concepts.summary: An entity represents a real or conceptual thing of interest, and attributes record the facts needed about each instance.

concepts.title: Identifiers
concepts.summary: An identifier is one attribute or a combination of attributes that uniquely distinguishes every entity instance.

concepts.title: Mapping a model to a table
concepts.summary: An entity maps to a table, its attributes map to columns, and its identifier maps to the primary key.

concepts.title: CREATE and entity integrity
concepts.summary: Table definitions choose column data types and constraints; a primary key must uniquely and non-nullably identify each row.

concepts.title: Projection and restriction
concepts.summary: SELECT chooses columns while WHERE restricts rows according to predicates such as comparisons, IN, and NOT IN.

concepts.title: Ordering and derived values
concepts.summary: ORDER BY controls report order, and expressions can calculate values from stored columns.

concepts.title: Aggregates and subqueries
concepts.summary: Aggregate functions summarize rows, and a subquery supplies a value or set used by an enclosing query.

concepts.title: Patterns and duplicate removal
concepts.summary: Regular-expression predicates find text patterns, while DISTINCT removes duplicate result rows.

concepts.title: Maintaining rows
concepts.summary: UPDATE changes selected rows and DELETE removes selected rows; omitting an appropriate WHERE condition can affect every row.
